::: {.why}
Daily mark-to-market is the difference between a futures position and every other leveraged position you will ever hold, and it is where the roll, the margin call and the funding cost all come from.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- List every cash flow between buying one E-mini S&P future and its expiry, including the ones that happen daily.
- Given a contango curve, say what the roll does to a long position's return and why it is not the same as losing money.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>55 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Watch the forwards and futures lecture from MIT 15.401. It covers the contract, margin, and the cost-of-carry relation in one sitting, which is exactly today's scope.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} On paper: you buy one E-mini S&P at 5,000 with the multiplier of 50 dollars per index point. The index closes at 4,960, then 5,020, then 5,010, then expires at 4,990. Write the variation margin cash flow on each of the four nights, and the total. Check that the total equals the multiplier times the change in index level.
:::
